newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES BARELY LOWER ON LATE SELLING.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES BARELY LOWER ON LATE SELLING.

text.p: Istanbul shares shed earlier gains in late selling on Wednesday as the market sought direction after parliament dropped on Tuesday a censure motion against the Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed at 1,509, down one point, or 0.07 percent from Tuesday when it gained 1.2 percent on expectations ahead of the motion vote. It brushed a high of 1,533 in the afternoon.
Trade volume rose to 15.35 trillion lira from Tuesday's 12.79 trillion.
"The index tested the 1,530 resistance after political uncertainty faded, but failed," said Sinan Paksoy from Prim securities.

The market's earlier expectation was that the motion filed by the secularist opposition would bring down Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-conservative coalition and a secularist pact would afterwards replace it.

MPs voted 271 against 265 to drop the motion which criticised the government for straying from the country's 73-year-old secularist path. A number of MPs from the government defected to the opposition in the vote, but Erbakan's alliance had the support of a small far-right Islamist party.
"I think the market will drift between 1,480 and 1,550 range. There will be a wait and see period," said Serdar Surer from Ekinciler securities.
The government has been ailing since the secularist military began pushing it in February to stamp out rising Islamist activism.
Brokers said there was no reaction to the news that a top prosecutor called on the constitutional court to outlaw Erbakan's Welfare Party for threatening the secularist state.

Of the 249 shares traded, 104 declined, 87 advanced and 58 were stable. The IMKB Industrial edged 0.07 percent lower to 1,454, the IMKB Services lost 1.08 percent to 1,373 and the IMKB Financial firmed 0.36 percent to 1,676.

Actives were led by utility Aktas Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 180,000, T.Isbank's C series shares, down 500 lira at 41,500 and commercial vehicle venture Anadolu Isuzu, up 4,000 lira at 74,000. They made up 15.6 percent of the total turnover.
